concept.name: Market-if-touched order
concept.definition: A conditional order to buy below (or sell above) the current market price that becomes a market order once the specified trigger ('touch') price trades. It is the mirror image of a stop order: a buy MIT is placed below the market and a sell MIT above it.
concept.intuition: It lets you say 'if the price falls to X, buy me in immediately at whatever is available' - a way to enter on a pullback with certainty of execution rather than certainty of price.
concept.mechanics: The order rests off-book at the broker or venue until the trigger price is touched (trade or quote, depending on venue convention); it is then released as a market order and fills at the best available prices. On CME Globex the analogous triggered market behavior is a market order released upon trigger.
concept.failure_modes: Because it becomes a market order, a touch during a thin or fast market can fill at a price far worse than the trigger price. A one-tick touch can also trigger entry immediately before the move fails.
concept.misconceptions: Traders often confuse MIT orders with stop orders; the placement is inverted (buy MIT below the market vs. buy stop above it). Nor does the touch price guarantee the fill price.
concept.example: With stock at $50, you place a buy MIT at $48. When a trade prints at $48, the order converts to a market order and fills at the best offer, perhaps $48.02.
